narration: In the spring of 1603, a Scottish king rode south to claim an English throne, and in doing so he did something no ruler had ever done before. He declared himself King of Great Britain. His name was James, and his life would reshape three kingdoms, one language, and the future of an empire.

narration: He was born on the nineteenth of June, fifteen sixty-six, in a small chamber high in Edinburgh Castle. His mother was Mary, Queen of Scots, the most glamorous and most doomed monarch in Europe. His father was Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley, a vain and dangerous young man.
search_terms: Mary Queen of Scots portrait painting

narration: Within eight months, his father was dead, strangled in an orchard after an explosion tore through his lodgings. Scandal engulfed the queen. She was forced to abdicate, and in July fifteen sixty-seven, a boy of thirteen months was crowned King James the Sixth of Scotland.
search_terms: James VI infant king portrait child

narration: He never saw his mother again. Instead he was raised by regents and guardians in the cold halls of Stirling Castle, a king who was also a prisoner of other men's ambitions. Four regents governed in his name. Three of them died violently.
search_terms: Stirling Castle great hall historic photograph

narration: His tutor was George Buchanan, one of the finest Latin scholars in Europe, and a man who beat learning into the boy without mercy. But it worked. James grew into perhaps the most intellectual monarch Britain has ever produced, fluent in Latin, Greek, and French, and a writer of real force.

Adolescence brought terror. In fifteen eighty-two he was seized by armed nobles in the Ruthven Raid and held captive for ten months. He learned early that a crown guarantees nothing, and that survival depended on patience, flattery, and the careful management of violent men.

In fifteen eighty-seven came the news he had long dreaded. His mother, a prisoner in England for nineteen years, was beheaded at Fotheringhay on the orders of Queen Elizabeth. James protested, but only briefly. The English succession was his prize, and he would not risk it for a mother he could not remember.
search_terms: Mary Queen of Scots execution engraving

narration: Two years later he married Anne of Denmark, a princess of fifteen. Storms scattered her fleet, and James sailed to Norway himself to fetch his bride, the only foreign journey of his life. Together they had seven children. Only three survived to adulthood.

James also wrote books, and they reveal a strange, brilliant, fearful mind. In Daemonologie he argued for the reality of witchcraft, helping unleash decades of witch trials. In Basilikon Doron and The True Law of Free Monarchies he set out the divine right of kings: that a monarch answers to God alone.

Then, on the twenty-fourth of March, sixteen hundred and three, Elizabeth the First died childless at Richmond. A ring was carried north at breakneck speed. Within days James was proclaimed king in London, and the crowns of Scotland and England rested at last on a single head.
search_terms: Queen Elizabeth I funeral procession engraving

narration: In October sixteen hundred and four he took a title no one had held before: King of Great Britain, France and Ireland. He commissioned a new flag, combining the cross of Saint George with the saltire of Saint Andrew. The Union Jack was born from his ambition.
search_terms: royal coat of arms James I engraving

narration: Not everyone welcomed him. On the fifth of November, sixteen hundred and five, a group of Catholic gentlemen packed thirty-six barrels of gunpowder beneath the House of Lords, intending to kill the king and his entire Parliament. Guy Fawkes was caught with a slow match in his pocket.
search_terms: Houses of Parliament old Westminster engraving

narration: His greatest monument was made of words. In sixteen eleven, after seven years of labour by forty-seven scholars, the Authorised Version of the Bible appeared. The King James Bible would shape English prose for four centuries, its rhythms echoing in speeches, novels, and songs to this day.
search_terms: King James Bible first edition page

narration: Abroad, his reign planted seeds he never saw grow. In sixteen hundred and seven, English colonists founded Jamestown in Virginia, naming it for their king. It became the first permanent English settlement in America, the fragile beginning of a world-spanning empire.

He called himself Rex Pacificus, the peacemaker king, and he ended England's long war with Spain. Yet he quarrelled endlessly with his Parliaments over money and power, and grew ever more dependent on handsome favourites, above all George Villiers, Duke of Buckingham.
search_terms: George Villiers Duke of Buckingham portrait

narration: James died on the twenty-seventh of March, sixteen twenty-five, worn out by illness, and was buried in Westminster Abbey. He left his son Charles a doctrine of absolute kingship that would cost Charles his head. The formal union of Britain took another century. But the idea was his, and it endured.
